angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,042,854 km at 80.50 pc = 0.17 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.4224 +/- 0.0286 mas (same row, RUWE 0.95): 80.50 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.499 +/- 0.077 solar radii from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-167 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract): 1,042,854 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.084 +/- 0.1 solar masses from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-167 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6310 +/- 170 K from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-167 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-167 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-167.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.121, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
